elements.quote: This review assessed the impact of pre-defined selection criteria on ECPR survival.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly describes the work as a review of pre-defined selection criteria on ECPR survival.

elements.quote: This review assessed the impact of pre-defined selection criteria on ECPR survival.

elements.quote: Adult patients (> 12 years) receiving ECPR were included.
elements.reason: Main inclusion criteria are provided, but explicit main exclusion criteria are not reported in the abstract text.

elements.quote: We searched Medline, Embase, and Evidence-Based Medicine Reviews for RCTs and observational studies published from January 2000 to June 2021.
elements.reason: The sources are named and a date range is provided, but the abstract does not explicitly state the last search date for each source.

elements.quote: Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS).
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the risk of bias/quality assessment method (NOS).

elements.quote: Meta-analysis and meta-regression were performed.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the synthesis/analysis approach used to present and synthesize results.

elements.quote: Results: 67 studies were included: 14 prospective and 53 retrospective.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies and summarizes relevant study characteristics (prospective vs retrospective).

elements.quote: Outcomes included overall and neurologically favourable survival. Results: 67 studies were included: 14 prospective and 53 retrospective... The number of inclusion criteria to select ECPR patients ( p = 0.292) and study design ( p = 0.962) was not associated with higher favourable neurological survival... amongst prospective studies, increased number of inclusion criteria was associated with improved outcomes in both OHCA and IHCA cohorts. (β = 0.12, p = 0.026) ... arrest to ECMO flow time was predictive of survival. (β = -0.023, p < 0.001).
elements.reason: Main outcome results are reported for overall/neurologically favourable survival in terms of associations, but the abstract does not provide the number of studies and participants for each outcome.
Although the abstract states that a meta-analysis was performed, it does not report a summary estimate with a confidence/credible interval for the main outcomes.

elements.quote: Conclusions: Prospective studies showed number of selection criteria and, in particular, arrest to ECMO time were associated with significant improved survival.
elements.reason: When comparing study types (prospective vs retrospective), the abstract indicates the direction of effect (prospective studies favored/associated with improved survival).

elements.quote: No RCTs were identified at time of search.
elements.reason: The abstract reports an important limitation related to included evidence (no RCTs identified).

elements.quote: Conclusions: Prospective studies showed number of selection criteria and, in particular, arrest to ECMO time were associated with significant improved survival. Well-designed prospective studies assessing the relative importance of criteria as well as larger efficacy studies are required to ensure appropriate application of what is a costly intervention.
elements.reason: The abstract provides interpretation and implications, including calls for further well-designed and larger studies.
The abstract does not specify the primary source of funding.
The abstract does not provide a register name and registration number.

elements.quote: However, reported outcomes vary considerably due to differing study designs and selection criteria.

elements.quote: We used the PICO (Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome) search format: Among adults with cardiac arrest in any setting (OHCA or IHCA) who qualify for ECPR by inclusion and exclusion parameters outlined ... (O). Contemporary studies from January 2000 to June 2021 were included. ... Studies with ≤ 5 patients receiving ECPR or studies that did not report the inclusion or exclusion criteria regarding the eligibility of ECPR or the timing of ECPR (i.e. during or after cardiac arrest) were excluded. The primary outcome of interest was favourable neurological outcomes on discharge, using study-specified definitions. ... Secondary outcome included absolute survival irrespective of neurological outcome to the end of each study period.
elements.reason: The eligibility criteria and key outcome timing (on discharge/end of study period) are specified using PICO, and eligible study designs are listed. However, the evidence does not clearly specify all study-characteristic components in the requested framework detail (e.g., comprehensive inclusion/exclusion specifics beyond what is quoted, and explicit setting/follow-up requirements beyond discharge/end of study).

elements.quote: Contemporary studies from January 2000 to June 2021 were included. Only English language studies were included.
elements.reason: The evidence specifies dissemination/report characteristics including date range (January 2000 to June 2021) and language (English). It does not explicitly mention publication/report status, so this is treated as present for the elements it covers.
No evidence is provided describing whether exclusions were distinguished based on outcomes not measured versus outcomes not reported.

elements.reason: The evidence identifies groups used for analyses/synthesis (prospective vs retrospective; IHCA vs OHCA) as pre-defined subgroups, which correspond to the review’s comparisons by study design and arrest location.
